text: Article · postmortem · The Cloudflare Blog Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang Kevin Flansburg, Michelle Chen (Cloudflare) · published 26 October 2026 In one line: From 27 August to 9 September 2026, Workers AI's GLM-5.3 endpoint advertised a 1,048,576-token window on a 681,280-token prefill KV pool; prompts over the pool took SGLang's rejection path, which in disaggregated mode still handed decode one token of cache, and decode answered from reserved pages still holding earlier requests' data.

text: The evidence, judged . read it (16 min) · SGLang security update: improving request isolation · discussion (182 points, 79 comments on 27 November 2026) The idea in one sentence: a serving engine reuses KV cache pages without clearing them, so isolation between users rests on its bookkeeping alone; Cloudflare accepted prompts its prefill pool could not hold, SGLang refused them internally yet still completed the handoff to decode with one token of real cache, and decode answered from reserved pages still holding earlier users' keys and values.
